A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INFER/UFC research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original INFER classification results, component ablations, cross-architecture evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original INFER results and ablations, including revised accuracy measurements and additional comparisons using static labels.

M1.justification: Both versions use additive UFC integration with class-spanning natural-image subsets, the same classification-plus-BN objective, ensemble-generated soft labels, and MixUp training. Algorithm and notation clarifications do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1k. Cross-architecture and sample-difficulty evaluations are retained. The new compensator illustrations do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds reported DSA and SeqMatch comparisons, beyond their earlier mentions in the text. Table 2 adds SRe2L* and G-VBSM*, evaluated using INFER's static-label strategy at matched compression ratios, while retaining the original dynamic-label baselines. These substantially extend the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: Table 2 introduces matched-compression static-label evaluation controls. Section 4.1 changes the stated dynamic-validation epoch scaling from 1/4 to 1/M. However, the appendix recipes remain unchanged, including 75 ImageNet dynamic-validation epochs despite M=3, so an actual change in executed training budgets is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds qualitative comparisons of compensators across architectures and initialization instances in Figures 6–7. Existing UFC and architecture-ensemble ablations have revised outcomes. The feature-duplication, decision-boundary, sample-difficulty, and label-divergence analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: For the ResNet18-plus-MobileNetv2 UFC ensemble at ipc=10, v2 Table 4 reports INFER+Dyn accuracy as 46.2 without uncertainty; v3 Table 3 adds ±0.4. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Static INFER results change extensively under retained stated training recipes. CIFAR-100/ResNet18 at ipc=50 changes from 65.1 to 62.8 in Table 1; ImageNet/ResNet50 at ipc=50 changes from 62.5 to 53.3 at the same 4.04% compression ratio in Table 2. Cross-architecture and ensemble results also change, and Figure 4(b)'s dynamic-label UFC gain at ipc=10 changes from 35.0 to 13.8 points. New baseline results are added, while main INFER+Dyn accuracy rows remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The distillation formulation, UFC objective, BN penalty, label-interpolation relation, and ensemble averaging remain mathematically equivalent. Separating the BN expression into its own numbered equation and clarifying intermediate-set notation introduce no new theoretical result. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central paradigm and efficiency contributions remain. The introduction revises its highlighted ImageNet/ResNet50 accuracy from 62.5% to 53.3% and removes the assertion that this performance requires no additional models. The abstract adds a specific 34.5-point advantage over static-label SRe2L at matched compression.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2's substantive limitations discussion concerning convergence and generalization beyond 1,000 classes and the separation of intra-class and inter-class optimization. It also removes the appendix interpretation of marginal or negative contributions from some labeling architectures. Conversely, it adds the interpretation that static labels suffice for simpler settings while dynamic labels provide stronger supervision for complex architectures.

D1.justification: v3 newly advertises code availability through a repository link and explicitly gives K=floor(ipc*C/(C+M)) for budget accounting. Ensemble-table captions now identify CIFAR-100. Hardware, architecture selections, and tabulated training recipes are retained; these disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu and Du's 2025 dataset-distillation survey and removes Kolesnikov et al.'s Big Transfer reference alongside the deleted ImageNet-21k limitation. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes local wording and notation corrections, updates author information, separates ablations from discussions in Section 4, and reorganizes appendices A–D into A.1–A.6. Most introductory and methodological prose is retained, so this is a limited narrative revision.

P2.justification: v3 adds two substantial compensator image grids, expands the comparison tables, and combines three training-recipe tables into one. It also relocates and resizes existing displays within the ICLR layout. The original appendix Figures 6–7 survive as Figures 8–9; their relocation is not new experimental content.

improvement.justification: The matched-compression controls, code-access information, and compensator illustrations improve transparency. However, v3 removes specific applicability limitations, retains broad superiority wording that needs qualification after the result revisions, and introduces an epoch-scaling statement inconsistent with the retained ImageNet recipe. These substantive benefits and reporting losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
